numbered_results.label: thm:main
numbered_results.section_title: The main theorem and its context
numbered_results.title: Two checker vertices certify the entire interval
numbered_results.statement: For every positive dimension n, every signature epsilon in {-1,1}^n and every real entrywise box [L,U], all matrices in the box are nonsingular and weakly sign regular with that signature if and only if its two checker vertices are.
numbered_results.scope: The target declaration proves the nontrivial implication for every real matrix in the box, with no extra premise. The reverse implication follows by applying the universal box property to each of the two vertices, whose membership is proved separately. The signature is indexed by minor order; no value at order zero is imposed. Proper minors may vanish, and fixed entries of both parities are allowed.

lean.name: IV01.twoCheckerVertices
lean.scope: Every n >= 1, every valid signature and entrywise L <= U, nonsingular sign-regular checker vertices, and every M in the box imply nonsingular sign regularity of M.

lean.name: IV01.checkerMinus_mem_box
lean.scope: Under entrywise L <= U, the minus checker vertex belongs to the box.

lean.name: IV01.checkerPlus_mem_box
lean.scope: Under entrywise L <= U, the plus checker vertex belongs to the box.

numbered_results.label: lem:inverse
numbered_results.title: Intervals with nonnegative endpoint inverses
numbered_results.statement: If real square P <= Q are nonsingular and both inverses are entrywise nonnegative, every P <= C <= Q is nonsingular and has entrywise nonnegative inverse.
numbered_results.scope: The formal declaration proves nonsingularity throughout the interval by a finite positive-supersolution argument. The additional conclusion C inverse >= 0 in this paper lemma is not the conclusion of that declaration and remains a paper statement here. The complete main theorem does not require that extra inverse conclusion as an unproved premise.

lean.name: IV01.inverse_positive_interval_nonsingular
lean.scope: For any finite dimension, arbitrary real square P,C,Q with nonsingular P,Q, nonnegative endpoint inverses and P <= C <= Q, the determinant of C is nonzero.

numbered_results.label: cor:nonsingular
numbered_results.title: Nonsingularity and cofactor signs in a checker interval
numbered_results.statement: For nonsingular sign-regular checker endpoints with common signature, every interval matrix is nonsingular, its determinant has the prescribed sign, and its minors of order n-1 have their prescribed weak sign; the n=1 order-zero convention is the empty determinant 1.
numbered_results.scope: Nonsingularity is proved directly by inBox_nonsingular. The complete stated nonempty-minor sign conclusions also follow from the final target, which proves all minor orders. The order-zero assertion uses the determinant of the empty matrix; SignRegular itself quantifies only over orders 1 through n. No separate bundled cofactor-sign theorem is claimed.

lean.name: IV01.inBox_nonsingular
lean.scope: A matrix in a real box with nonsingular sign-regular checker endpoints has nonzero determinant.

lean.name: IV01.twoCheckerVertices
lean.scope: The full theorem gives every prescribed nonempty minor sign, including the determinant and order n-1 when n >= 2.

numbered_results.label: lem:staircase
numbered_results.title: Staircase support of a nonsingular TN2 matrix
numbered_results.statement: A nonsingular nonnegative real square matrix with nonnegative two-minors has positive diagonal. Zeros above and below the diagonal propagate northeast and southwest. Each row and column support is a nonempty interval containing its diagonal position, and row support endpoints are nondecreasing.
numbered_results.scope: Positive diagonal and both zero-propagation statements are explicit Lean conclusions. The paper packages their support-interval and monotone-endpoint consequences in set language; no single bundled declaration for that wording is cited. Subsequent formal arguments use the zero-propagation consequences directly.

lean.name: IV01.diagonal_pos_of_nonsingular
lean.scope: Nonnegative entries, TP2 and nonzero determinant imply positivity of every diagonal entry.

lean.name: IV01.northeast_zero
lean.scope: For a linearly ordered square matrix with nonnegative entries, TP2 and positive diagonal, an above-diagonal zero forces the northeast rectangle to vanish.

lean.name: IV01.southwest_zero
lean.scope: The corresponding below-diagonal zero forces the southwest rectangle to vanish.

numbered_results.label: prop:ordertwo
numbered_results.title: The first two minor orders throughout the box
numbered_results.statement: Under the nonsingular common-signature checker-endpoint hypotheses, every matrix in the interval has the prescribed weak signs at minor orders one and two.
numbered_results.scope: Separate declarations prove the entry signs and all increasing two-minor signs. The order-two assertion is vacuous when two increasing rows or columns do not exist; no restriction on dimension or zero entries is introduced.

lean.name: IV01.entry_sign_in_box
lean.scope: Sign-regular checker endpoints and box membership imply the prescribed order-one sign at every entry.

lean.name: IV01.order_two_in_box
lean.scope: Every increasing pair of rows and columns has the prescribed weak two-minor sign throughout the box.

numbered_results.label: lem:corner
numbered_results.title: A positive zero two-minor forces a rank-one corner
numbered_results.statement: In a nonsingular TN2 matrix with common third-minor sign eta, a positive vanishing two-minor on i<j and k<l forces an NW or SE rank-one corner when eta=-1, and an NE or SW corner when eta=+1. The possible orientation is unique for those anchor indices.
numbered_results.scope: RankOneOn records an outer-product factorization on the indicated corner, hence rank at most one; the positive anchor makes its rank exactly one. The common-orientation declaration prevents opposite orientations even for two different nonsingular matrices with the same indices. The formal existence lemma needs positivity of three anchor entries; the fourth follows from the vanishing determinant.

lean.name: IV01.rankOneCorner_of_positive_zero_two
lean.scope: Under TP2, nonsingularity, signed three-minors and eta in {-1,1}, a positive vanishing anchor lies in one of the two prescribed outer-product corners.

lean.name: IV01.common_corner_orientation
lean.scope: Two nonsingular matrices with the same anchor indices and eta, each having a candidate corner, have a common orientation.

numbered_results.label: lem:twozeros
numbered_results.title: Only the two extreme corners can be zero
numbered_results.statement: A nonsingular TN2 matrix of order at least three whose three-minors are nonpositive can have zero entries only at (1,N) and (N,1).
numbered_results.scope: The formal conclusion describes the first and last index by their order properties, so it agrees with either zero-based or one-based notation. Its hypotheses imply the paper result; no strict positivity assumption on all entries is added.

lean.name: IV01.zero_only_extreme_corners
lean.scope: Under nonnegative entries, TP2, nonsingularity and nonpositive three-minors, a zero is in the first-row/last-column or last-row/first-column position.

numbered_results.label: lem:middle
numbered_results.title: A zero in the middle column excludes a negative three-minor
numbered_results.statement: Every real 3 by 3 TN2 matrix with a zero entry in its middle column has nonnegative determinant.
numbered_results.scope: The complete three-dimensional statement is formal, including singular matrices and any of the three possible middle-column zero positions.

lean.name: IV01.det_nonneg_of_middle_column_zero
lean.scope: For a nonnegative TP2 matrix of order three, existence of a zero in column 1 in zero-based indexing implies nonnegative determinant.

numbered_results.label: lem:schur
numbered_results.section_title: Signed Schur complements and rank completion
numbered_results.title: Signed Schur determinant and rank identities
numbered_results.statement: For an invertible pivot H=Z[P,Q] of size p, the signed Schur minor on complementary increasing I,J is det Z[P union I,Q union J]/det H. Every rectangular extension of the pivot has rank p plus its Schur residual rank. The complete Schur complement is nonsingular when Z is.
numbered_results.scope: The formal identities use explicit index maps and sorting permutations. They allow nonprincipal, noncontiguous and empty pivots. The nonsingularity declaration requires the complete bordered determinant to be nonzero, supplied by nonsingularity of the full matrix when the index maps cover it.

lean.name: IV01.signedSchurAt_sorted_det
lean.scope: The signed Schur determinant equals the increasing bordered minor divided by the nonzero pivot determinant, with all ordering signs included.

lean.name: IV01.schurAt_sorted_rank
lean.scope: For rectangular residual row and column maps, the sorted bordered rank is p plus the residual Schur rank.

lean.name: IV01.schurAt_nonsingular
lean.scope: Nonzero pivot and bordered determinants imply nonzero determinant of the square Schur residual.

numbered_results.label: lem:rank-obstruction
numbered_results.section_title: Signed Schur complements and rank completion
numbered_results.title: Rank obstruction for a negative normalized third-order sign
numbered_results.statement: For a nonsingular sign-regular Z, 0 <= p <= n-3, normalized third-order sign -1, and a rectangle of actual rank t <= p with at least p rows, (row_count-p)(column_count-t) <= 2. In particular, rank <= p excludes sizes at least (p+2) by (p+2) and (p+3) by (p+1).
numbered_results.scope: The cited Lean theorem proves (row_count-p)(column_count-p) <= 2, which is sufficient to exclude both displayed sizes. The stronger t-dependent inequality stated in the paper is not asserted by this declaration when t<p. Completion of a deficient pivot is included; no equality of the original rank with p is assumed.

lean.name: IV01.negative_third_rank_rectangle_bound
lean.scope: For increasing rows, injective columns, rank <= p and the stated signature hypotheses, the natural-number product (row_count-p)(column_count-p) is at most two.

numbered_results.label: lem:permanent
numbered_results.section_title: From a bad minor to a permanent rank bound
numbered_results.title: Interior zeros and rank bounds persist throughout the box
numbered_results.statement: Assume all minors through order k-1 have prescribed weak signs throughout the box. Any such minor vanishing at a relative-interior matrix vanishes everywhere. A submatrix of rank s <= k-2 at that point has rank at most s everywhere.
numbered_results.scope: The formal zero statement needs only a common nonzero signed lower bound for the particular minor. The rank statement needs the common sign at order s+1. Relative interior refers to the genuinely free coordinates and includes singleton boxes.

lean.name: IV01.minor_zero_on_box
lean.scope: An increasing minor with a common weak sign on a real box and zero value at a relative-interior point is zero throughout the box.

lean.name: IV01.rectangle_rank_bound_on_box
lean.scope: A rectangular rank bound at a relative-interior point holds on the whole box when all increasing minors of the next order have the same nonzero weak sign.

numbered_results.label: lem:fekete
numbered_results.section_title: From a bad minor to a permanent rank bound
numbered_results.title: The three-term determinantal identity
numbered_results.statement: For k rows, any k-1 selected rows, a k-column set with extremes a,c and core S, and a missing a<b<c, the product Delta(J)d(S union {b}) equals the sum of the two smaller-span determinant products in equation (6.2). No rank hypothesis is needed.
numbered_results.scope: The algebraic identity is proved over a commutative ring and specialized by submatrix maps. To match the paper, use increasing row and column maps in the displayed order and q=k-2. The formal identity itself does not need injectivity or rank assumptions.

lean.name: IV01.fekete_three_term_submatrix
lean.scope: For any matrix over a commutative ring and the specified deletion maps on q+3 columns, the three determinant products satisfy exactly the Fekete relation.

numbered_results.label: lem:solid
numbered_results.section_title: From a bad minor to a permanent rank bound
numbered_results.title: Solid minors have the prescribed sign
numbered_results.statement: Assume the checker endpoints have the prescribed signature and every minor through order k-1 has its prescribed weak sign throughout the box. Then each solid k-minor has its prescribed weak sign throughout the box.
numbered_results.scope: The formal statement uses k=q+2 and consecutive row and column maps. It requires only the preceding minor order throughout the box, together with sign-regular checker endpoints; endpoint nonsingularity is unnecessary for this isolated step.

lean.name: IV01.solid_minor_sign
lean.scope: For every consecutive minor of order q+2 that fits inside the matrix, the endpoint signs and all order-(q+1) signs on the box imply its signed nonnegativity.

numbered_results.label: lem:rectangle
numbered_results.section_title: From a bad minor to a permanent rank bound
numbered_results.title: A bad minor yields a permanent deficient rectangle
numbered_results.statement: If a wrong-sign k-minor exists under the lower-order sign hypotheses, choose a relative-interior wrong-sign minor of minimum total row and column span. After possible transposition, its k by open-interior-column rectangle has rank r=k-2, at least r+1 columns, and rank at most r throughout the box; its r core columns form a basis.
numbered_results.scope: A separate continuity declaration moves a strict wrong sign to relative interior. The finite minimum-span construction and permanent-rank declaration then give the rectangle or its transpose. Independence of the core columns comes from the nonzero target determinant and is used in the proof; the final existential contract records the exact rank and permanent upper bound.

lean.name: IV01.exists_interior_bad_minor
lean.scope: A strict wrong-sign minor at any box point persists at a relative-interior point.

lean.name: IV01.rank_interior_eq_of_minimal_bad
lean.scope: For an order q+2 bad minor minimal in column span and common lower signs, the whole open-interior-column rectangle has rank exactly q.

lean.name: IV01.exists_permanent_bad_rectangle_or_transpose
lean.scope: From an interior bad minor, correct solid signs and common lower signs on the box, produces the bad rectangle, cardinality and permanent rank bound, in the original or transposed orientation.

numbered_results.label: lem:essential
numbered_results.section_title: From a bad minor to a permanent rank bound
numbered_results.title: One-entry variation forces an essential row or column
numbered_results.statement: If a rectangular matrix F has rank r >= 1 and sufficiently small positive and negative perturbations at a single entry preserve rank at most r, its affected row or column is essential: deletion drops rank by one.
numbered_results.scope: The formal theorem is stronger: one nonzero entry perturbation with rank at most the original rank suffices, over any field and finite row and column types. The box application supplies such a perturbation from a free coordinate at a relative-interior matrix.

lean.name: IV01.essential_row_or_column_of_rank_single
lean.scope: For arbitrary finite matrices over a field and any t != 0, rank(F+tEij) <= rank(F) implies that deleting row i or column j reduces rank exactly by one.

lean.name: IV01.essential_line_of_free_entry
lean.scope: A free entry in a rectangle of maximal rank at a relative-interior box point belongs to an essential row or column.

numbered_results.label: ex:singular
numbered_results.title: Singular endpoints
numbered_results.statement: The displayed totally nonnegative singular 3 by 3 checker endpoints have a midpoint two-minor -1/4. Direct sums with an identity preserve the counterexample in every dimension n >= 3.
numbered_results.scope: Rational computation enumerates all minors of the displayed endpoints at dimensions 3 and 5 and verifies the midpoint minor -1/4. The extension to every n >= 3 is the paper direct-sum argument; no Lean declaration for this example or that extension is claimed.

numbered_results.label: ex:signature
numbered_results.title: A common signature is necessary
numbered_results.statement: Two checker-comparable strictly sign-regular matrices of order two with signatures (+1,-1) and (+1,+1) have determinants -3 and 3, while their midpoint is singular.
numbered_results.scope: The exact program checks all endpoint minors, checker order and the three determinant values for this two-dimensional example. The statement has no asserted identity-block extension.

numbered_results.label: ex:ordinary
numbered_results.title: Ordinary lower and upper bounds do not suffice
numbered_results.statement: The displayed strictly totally positive 2 by 2 lower and upper bounds have determinants 1 and 3 but contain a matrix with determinant -4. Identity-block sums give the same obstruction with nonsingular totally nonnegative ordinary bounds for every n >= 2.
numbered_results.scope: The exact program checks dimensions 2 and 5, all endpoint minors, interval membership and the bad two-minor -4. The every-dimension conclusion is the paper direct-sum argument; it is not inferred from the two finite sizes.

numbered_results.label: ex:degenerate
numbered_results.title: A degenerate four-parameter box
numbered_results.statement: An explicitly specified rational 5 by 5 box with four free entries of width 1/8 has checker-vertex signature (+1,+1,-1,+1,-1), exactly one zero minor of order two at each vertex, fixed entries of both parities and a fixed positive-entry directed cycle. Every matrix in the box has the same nonsingular sign-regular signature.
numbered_results.scope: The program verifies the seed inverse, all endpoint minor counts, unique zero pattern, four free coordinates, cycle and signature exclusion, and enumerates all minors at all 16 ordinary vertices. Multiaffine interpolation gives this finite box from those vertex checks; the full main theorem also applies. No Lean specialization containing these rational matrices is claimed.

ingredients.title: A fixed interior rectangle
ingredients.statement: An alleged order p+3 bad minor with fixed interior-column rectangle of rank p+1 is excluded by a common rank-one corner, rank lifting and the affine midpoint argument.
ingredients.scope: The fixed-case contract includes all endpoint, lower-order, relative-interior and permanent-rank hypotheses obtained earlier. It is proved, and the main target supplies this theorem to the general induction. No exclusion contract remains as an assumption of the target.

lean.name: IV01.fixedRectangleExcluded
lean.scope: Proves the entire FixedRectangleExcluded proposition for every dimension, signature, pivot order and qualifying box.

ingredients.title: A free rectangle with negative third-order sign
ingredients.statement: An alleged order p+3 bad minor with a nonfixed rank-(p+1) interior rectangle and normalized third-order sign -1 is excluded by an essential line and the forbidden rectangle sizes.
ingredients.scope: The rank argument covers residual endpoint rank strictly below p. The proved contract takes the earlier endpoint and lower-order signs, interior matrix, rank certificate and negative Schur third-order sign.

lean.name: IV01.negativeNonfixedRectangleExcluded
lean.scope: Proves SignedNonfixedRectangleExcluded (-1), with no additional unproved premise.

ingredients.title: A free rectangle with positive third-order sign
ingredients.statement: An alleged order p+3 bad minor with a nonfixed rank-(p+1) interior rectangle and normalized third-order sign +1 is excluded by Schur elimination at the interior matrix and the middle-column zero argument.
ingredients.scope: Both essential-row and essential-column alternatives are proved. The pivot is local to the interior matrix; fixedness or invertibility of that same pivot at either endpoint is not required.

lean.name: IV01.positiveNonfixedRectangleExcluded
lean.scope: Proves SignedNonfixedRectangleExcluded 1, with both essential-line alternatives included.

checks.scope: Exact rational arithmetic checks all four displayed examples, including all 16 ordinary vertices of the four-parameter box. The singular and ordinary-bound identity extensions are instantiated only at dimensions 3 and 5, and 2 and 5, respectively. The whole verification entry point also requires each of the four altered examples to fail under both normal and optimized Python.

scope: The full all-dimensional interval theorem is formalized by IV01.twoCheckerVertices. It quantifies over arbitrary real entries and all prescribed signatures, allows zero proper minors and fixed entries of both parities, and concludes nonsingularity as well as every weak minor sign.

Paper Lemma 3.1 also states inverse nonnegativity throughout an inverse-positive interval. The cited isolated Lean result proves nonsingularity only. This difference does not add an assumption to the main declaration.
Paper Lemma 5.2 has a bound depending on the actual deficient rank t. The isolated Lean bound uses p in both factors, which suffices for the two forbidden sizes used by the complete proof.

The target states the checker-vertex-to-box implication. Its converse follows by the two proved checker-vertex membership facts. Zero-based matrix indices preserve checker parity when both indices are shifted to the paper convention.

The paper examples and their all-dimensional direct-sum explanations are not separate Lean theorems. The rational programs check the stated finite instances; the universal theorem is supplied independently by the full Lean proof.

This correspondence checker verifies references and the complete numbered-result inventory. It does not compile Lean or establish mathematical equivalence from prose; use the separate build and axiom commands in VERIFICATION.md.

The theorem concerns real square entrywise Cartesian boxes and one common signature at nonsingular checker endpoints. It gives no unconditional singular-endpoint theorem, no replacement by the ordinary lower and upper bounds, and no polynomial-time claim for evaluating all required endpoint minors.
